messages:
oncall-bot: Pager — P2: continuous-batching latency spike detected on region-us-west-2 (kv-cache growth + queueing). 2xx->5xx tail increase. Alert ID: cb-1943210000
Alex R: got it, I'm oncall. hitting the dashboard now. seeing a sharp climb in pending queue depth on runtime pool A.
Maria G: I’m seeing KV cache evictions spike at the same time. lots of short-lived prefixes. could be a prefix storm from a customer job.
Alex R: curious — is it pure eviction churn or memory growth?
Maria G: memory stable but active evictions/sec up 12x. that means cache thrashing; continuous batching holding onto more inflight KV entries and blocking microbatch flush.
Leo T: latency tail looks like microbatches are waiting for slots. requests pile up -> batch size grows -> increased latency -> more requests queue -> perf cliff. classic feedback loop.
Samir P: any signs of traffic coroutines with identical prefixes? trace sample: `trace_id=tb-194321-7f` shows many requests with same prefix key for a 1-token warmup endpoint.
Alex R: ok mitigation plan attempt 1: throttle requests per-prefix at router (quick), and reduce continuous batching window to break big microbatches.
Alex R: applying config change to routing: `curl -X POST https://control-plane/api/routers/us-west-2/config -d '{"per_prefix_rate_limit": "50/s"}'` — will roll to 10% first.
deploy-bot: deploy started for router-config/us-west-2 at 1943210065 (canary 10%). CI checks passed.
Maria G: while that rolls, we should patch runtime batching: set `continuous_batch.max_delay_ms` 20->5 and enable `microbatch.jitter_ms=3` to reduce synchronized admissions. small change, hotpatch-able.
Leo T: +1. Also cap `microbatch.max_items` from 64->16 to prevent runaway big batches. that gives predictable tail.
Samir P: any customer impact? canary rolling?
Alex R: initial impact: overall 99th latency dropped from 2.8s -> 900ms in canary nodes. error rate on affected cluster dropped from 4.8%->1.1%. customer-facing support: two large tenants on Dedicated saw transient 5xxs for 3–7 minutes.
Maria G: pushing runtime hotfix to the rest of the pool now. command: `kubectl -n runtime patch deploy cb-runtime --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"hotfix":"194321-hotfix-01"}}}}}'`
deploy-bot: hotfix rollout triggered at 1943210120. progressing 25% -> 50% -> 100%.
Alex R: monitoring. queue depth normalizing. KV eviction rate down ~70%. looks like batching window reduction helped break the cascade.
Leo T: note: we saw a small regression in throughput for some low-latency single-token calls ~8% drop; acceptable vs tail improvement.
Samir P: logged customer impact summary for CSM: 2 Dedicated tenants with 3–7m of elevated error rates, hosted customers saw small latency spikes but no sustained errors.
Alex R: escalation notes: root cause appears to be a workload that generates many near-identical prefixes under high concurrency, causing KV cache churn which amplifies continuous batching queueing.
Maria G: follow-ups: 1) ask model-onboarding to throttle prefix-heavy clients; 2) add automated per-prefix backpressure at router; 3) add safer defaults: `max_delay_ms=10`, `max_items=32`, `jitter_ms` enabled by default; 4) add an alert for eviction-rate->batch-pending correlation.
Alex R: handing off to Leo T — I'm off in 15. leaf checklist in thread.
Leo T: taking over. current state: stable w/ hotfix fully rolled, canary verified. I’ll keep pager coverage for next 2 hours and run a playback to reproduce.
Leo T: action items I’ll own: reproducer run, adjust default config in repo, write an emergency test that simulates prefix storms, update runbook.
Samir P: I’ll prepare the customer-facing postmortem blurb for CSMs and draft email for the two affected tenants.
oncall-bot: Reminder: next oncall handoff scheduled at 1943215400.
Alex R: quick note to SRE: we should consider a runtime metric `microbatch.wait_time_p90` and a composite `eviction*pending_queue` alert to catch this earlier.
Maria G: adding to backlog and tagging in ticketing system. ticket: INF-194321 (created).
Leo T: summarizing before I close out: mitigation = router per-prefix rate limit + runtime hotpatch (max_delay_ms=5, jitter_ms=3, max_items=16) rolled to 100%. impact = brief 5xx spike for two tenants; 99th latency improved across cluster. next steps = tests + config defaults + per-prefix backpressure + runbook updates.
Alex R: thanks team. closing incident channel once docs + postmortem draft posted. :thumbsup:
